_meta.label: Mucinous carcinoma
_meta.scope: Every efficacy figure is copied from data/trials_moc.json; toxicity from data/tox.json or data/tox_histotypes.json; label rules from data/labels.json or data/labels_histotypes.json. "base" inherits drugs, drug classes, tox_ref, PFS text, risk_rules and ledger_rules from the named HGSC record.
_meta.tier_reading: The only MOC randomised trial (mEOC/GOG-0241) closed at 50 of 330 patients and is uninformative for decision-making, so every active regimen is tier 6 and the ranking within tier 6 is toxicity plus fit. Tier 7 = classes that never enrolled mucinous carcinoma (PARPi, mirvetuximab, relacorilant, checkpoint inhibitors) or showed no benefit with added toxicity.
_meta.pathology_gate: Confirm the ovarian primary before choosing systemic therapy: in both randomised first-line datasets with central review, most 'mucinous ovarian' cases were reinterpreted as metastatic (GOG-0241 confirmed 18/40; GOG five-arm 57–63% metastatic). The ranker shows a warning until primary_confirmed is ticked.
patient_fields_added: her2 (existing field; the one biomarker that changes options in MOC)

regimens.name: Observation after complete staging (stage I, expansile pattern)

os.median: NCDB stage I MOC: adjusted OS HR 1.18 (0.85–1.64) with chemotherapy; stage IC IPTW HR 0.88 (0.60–1.31); SEER cause-specific HR 1.296 — no registry shows a benefit

pfs.text: Algera 2024: stage I recurrences 5% (expansile) vs 14% (infiltrative), P=0.011; Hollis 2021: stage I grade 1 10-yr DSS 95.3% with or without chemotherapy

qualifiers: No randomised trial has tested adjuvant chemotherapy in MOC; the pooled ICON1/ACTION death count (10/90 vs 22/90) has no mucinous HR and predates primary-vs-metastatic review
The expansile/infiltrative split changes the prior risk (5% vs 14% recurrence), not the proven effect of chemotherapy

prefer_when.reason: Expansile stage I: recurrence ~5%, adjuvant chemotherapy given in 5% of the Dutch registry
Stage I: no survival association with chemotherapy in NCDB or SEER

risk_rules.reason: Infiltrative stage I: recurrence 14% and lethal recurrences mainly infiltrative; no source compares chemotherapy vs observation within this group
Stage II sits in the GOG-0241 'advanced' population; registry no-benefit data are stage I only

pfs.text: GOG-157 mucinous (n=31): recurrence HR 1.68 (0.30–9.29) for 6 vs 3 cycles — more cycles did not help

qualifiers: If chemotherapy is given for infiltrative stage IC–II, three cycles is the only schedule with any mucinous comparison (and it favoured fewer cycles)

prefer_when.reason: Infiltrative pattern carries the recurrence risk that makes adjuvant chemotherapy worth discussing

risk_rules.reason: GOG-157 mucinous subgroup numerically favoured 3 cycles; 6 adds neurotoxicity

os.median: GOG-0241: Pac-Carbo (±bev) median OS 27.7 mo vs Oxal-Cape (±bev) 33.9 mo, HR 0.77 for Oxal-Cape, P=0.48; confirmed-MOC Pac-Carbo 29.3 mo

qualifiers: Platinum–taxane response is poor in advanced MOC across series (ORR 26.3% vs 64.9% serous; pooled RCT PFS HR 2.10 and OS HR 2.66 vs serous) — the regimen is the default, not a demonstrated success

risk_rules.reason: Primary MOC not confirmed: most locally diagnosed 'mucinous ovarian' cases were metastatic on central review; a GI primary changes the regimen

risk_rules.reason: Oxaliplatin §2.2: persistent G2 neuropathy → reduce; persistent G3 → consider discontinuing; G4 → discontinue. Baseline G2 leaves little margin
